output.contract_title: SaaS Subscription Agreement with Enterprise Partner 006 LLC

clauses.clause_text: Customer shall pay all undisputed invoice amounts within thirty (30) days of invoice date.
Vendor shall notify Customer in writing within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of any confirmed Data Breach.
Neither party shall limit its liability under this Agreement for any claims whatsoever.
Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon providing thirty (30) days prior written notice.
This Agreement renews on an annual basis unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 30 days prior.

extraction_notes: Document extracted once for downstream policy comparison

mandatory_requirements.description: Aggregate liability cap must not exceed 12 months of total fees paid or payable.
Customer must have the right to terminate for convenience with no more than 30 days prior written notice.

ambiguities_in_policy: The phrase "12 months of total fees paid or payable" does not clarify whether the calculation is based on annual fees, monthly fees multiplied by 12, or a rolling 12‑month period.

The termination clause states "no more than 30 days prior written notice" but does not specify how partial days are treated, whether business days or calendar days apply, or if the notice period starts upon receipt or dispatch of the notice.

deviations.supporting_evidence: The liability clause (CLS-0006-LIAB) caps aggregate liability at 18 months of the total fees payable, which exceeds the policy maximum of 12 months.
deviations.recommended_remediation: Amend the liability clause to limit the aggregate liability to no more than 12 months of total fees paid or payable, or add explicit carve‑outs that are permissible under policy.

risk_findings.ambiguity_description: The term 'undisputed' is not defined and there is no dispute resolution process, creating uncertainty around when payment is due.
Obligation to notify is placed solely on Vendor; terms 'becoming aware' and 'confirmed Data Breach' are undefined, leading to potential delays in breach reporting.
Clause removes any liability caps for both parties, exposing each to unlimited financial exposure for any claim.
Automatic annual renewal lacks provisions for price adjustments, service changes, or review, creating risk of unintended continuation under outdated terms.

inconsistencies.description: Clause 12.1 allows either party to terminate the Agreement for convenience with 30 days' written notice at any time, while Clause 12.4 provides an automatic annual renewal unless a non‑renewal notice is given at least 30 days before the renewal date. If a party issues a termination notice within the 30‑day window preceding the renewal date, it is unclear whether the termination supersedes the renewal provision or whether the renewal still occurs, creating a temporal conflict between termination and renewal mechanisms.

Clause 10.1 states that neither party shall limit its liability for any claims, creating unlimited liability. This may conflict with the organization’s standard policy (POL-CORP-SEC-01 version 2.4), which typically imposes liability caps, potentially rendering the clause unenforceable under corporate policy.
